Example goals might include reducing the total amount of refrigerant across a building portfolio or reducing refrigerant leaks across the portfolio by a certain percentage. Step 3. Complete a Refrigeration Equipment Inventory To address refrigerant management goals, conduct a refrigerant inventory of the equipment to help determine current refrigerant use and future needs. The first and most time-consuming part of this step is a systematic walk-through of the site with a focus on the equipment, also referred to as assets, covered in Table 2. Ideally, each asset would have a permanent tag (see Figure 3) to identify it easily. In addition, as refrigerant consuming equipment is purchased (e.g., a new HVAC unit), it should be tagged and inventoried, which may require coordination between departments. This list can be created and maintained by facilities, accounting, or another appropriate office and be updated by a facilities employee. The information in Table 2 can be stored in software designed for refrigerant management or asset management, or in a spreadsheet. Although Table 2 is designed for an individual building, a column for building names could be added so that assets in multiple buildings can be organized by, for example, refrigerant type or equipment age. Some equipment has multiple refrigerant loops, often called refrigerant circuits. For example, a two-stage air conditioner may have two compressors and two refrigerant circuits—essentially it is two air conditioners housed in the same unit. Ideally, each circuit would be identified, maintained, and tracked separately as different maintenance assets, a strategy that also helps isolate problems when a system component has repeated issues.
